sender.en: A “customer care” or “refund desk” number found on Google search

name.en: Fake customer care number from a web search

how.en: You search online for the helpline of an airline, bank, e-commerce site, cab app or courier, and call a number on a fake page or listing. The “executive” promises a refund or fix, then asks you to install a screen-sharing app like AnyDesk, fill a form with card details, share an OTP or scan a QR code. Money is taken from your account instead of refunded. Official helplines are only on the company's own app or website.

text.en: You call a helpline number found through a web search.
The agent asks you to install AnyDesk or another screen-sharing app.
You are asked for an OTP, UPI PIN or card details to process a refund.
They keep you on the call while money is taken.

Caller: Thank you for calling the airline refund desk. Your cancellation refund is stuck. Please download AnyDesk and give me the nine-digit code, then open your bank app so I can push the refund to your account.

fake helpline agent wanted remote access
refund desk asked for screen sharing
Helpline numbers from search results, ads or social media.
Requests for screen sharing, OTP or UPI PIN.
A refund that needs you to pay or scan.
Find helplines only in the company's official app or website.
Never install screen-sharing apps for a stranger.
If money was taken, call your bank and 1930 immediately.
